nothing from internal/daemon -- only SignCommand and FakeSpawner

  three-way EthosVersion duplication rsc flagged is now two

  unavoidable floor: one lives in Go, one in Make, and nothing bridges
  that gap cleanly. Collapsing further by adding a version constant to
  internal/daemon's own production code (the only place both
  pipeline_test.go and daemontest could reach without recreating the
  cycle) was considered and rejected -- it leaks a test-tooling version
  pin into the production package's public surface to save one string
  literal that only ever appears in a human-facing error message.
- harness_test.go (package daemon_test) now calls testenv.EthosOrFatal/
  GenOwnerKey/BuildPGPSignedMessage instead of the daemontest re-exports.

handler_test.go's/signature_test.go's own local RFC822/GPG builders are
untouched -- replacing those with the newly-relocated testenv helpers
is a further, larger deduplication this round's write-set doesn't cover
and isn't required for correctness; noted as a low-priority follow-on.
EOF

tool_input.message:
Round 2 is open now — you were right that I hadn't reflected/advanced. `ethos mission advance m-2026-08-31-002` done, so submit your round-2 result when the item below is handled.

**Your round-2 work verified on my side:** all four gpg sites converted, fixed once at `gpgBinary` rather than four times, which is the right level. Your TESTING.md scoping call is also right — keeping the rule as the repo-wide standard and citing beadle-hi4n as the outstanding gap is better than narrowing the bullet, because narrowing would read as "t.Skip is fine elsewhere by policy," and it isn't; it's fine elsewhere only because nobody's fixed it yet. And I agree with declining to leak a test-tooling version pin into `internal/daemon`'s production surface to save a string that only appears in an error message.

**One residual counterexample, and I'm raising it because we just rejected a round for precisely this shape.**

`internal/daemon/runner_test.go:35`:

```go
if src == "" {
    t.Skipf("binary %q not found in /usr/bin or /bin", name)
}
```

That is a `t.Skip` on a missing external dependency, inside `internal/daemon`. Your sub-clause is accurate — "every `gpg`- or `ethos`-dependent test under `internal/daemon` now fails with the install remedy" is true. But the headline above it reads "**No `t.Skip` on a missing external dependency, ever — the standard for every test in this repo, not only `internal/daemon`**", and a reader will take the combination to mean `internal/daemon` is now clean. It isn't, by that rule's own definition.

I don't think this is the same severity as the gpg omission — it's a system utility, present on any real dev box and every CI runner, not a tool a developer must install. But we just spent a round establishing that a document must not claim a property the repo lacks, and shipping a smaller instance of that would be incoherent.

**Your call between two resolutions, and I'll take either with reasoning:**

- Convert it. If the binaries are POSIX utilities that exist everywhere the suite runs, `t.Fatalf` is safe and makes the claim true without qualification. Check what's actually in that `binaries` slice before deciding — if any entry is genuinely optional on a supported platform, this option is wrong.
- Keep the skip and name it. If there's a real reason a supported environment might legitimately lack one of those binaries, that's a principled exception — but then TESTING.md must say so explicitly rather than leaving a reader to discover the counterexample.

What I don't want is the claim standing unqualified with the counterexample unmentioned.

While you're deciding, sanity-check whether any *other* `t.Skip`/`t.Skipf` exists anywhere under `internal/daemon` that I've missed — I grepped and found only this one plus two comments, but confirm rather than take my word.

`make check`, commit, do not push. Then submit: `ethos mission result m-2026-08-31-002 --file .tmp/missions/results/m-2026-08-31-002-round2.yaml`. Report your resolution and reasoning.
